listing.title: EnergyMag year-round virtual research internship
listing.description: Unpaid remote research internship for high-school sophomores, juniors and seniors. Quarter-time placements run year-round for 1–9 months at approximately 8 hours per week. Research renewable-energy storage companies, technologies or markets with a mentor. Apply through the form on the official page; selection and places are not guaranteed.
listing.eligibility: High-school sophomores, juniors and seniors; GPA over 3.25 and at least one honors science or honors English class, with exceptions considered by EnergyMag. A writing sample, academic record or interview may be requested.

text: Quarter-time internships are available all year round

listing.title: building-U remote high-school team internship
listing.description: Free-to-join remote internship intake for grades 9–12, open year-round worldwide. Join student teams working on research, marketing, coding, business development or social media. Placements require at least three months. The official page asks applicants to email an introduction, with a resume if available; compensation is not stated.
listing.eligibility: Currently enrolled in grade 9, 10, 11 or 12. Teams include students from Canada and around the world. Email the address on the official page to join an information session and discuss a suitable team.
listing.cost: Free to join; compensation not stated

text: ONLINE so you can join our team from wherever you are in the world

listing.title: LaunchX Online Entrepreneurship — Summer 2027
listing.description: Tuition-based online entrepreneurship program for high-school students aged 14–18, July 5–August 6, 2027. The page lists US$7,495, while its FAQ quotes a starting price of US$6,495; confirm the current price with LaunchX. Financial awards and separate application fees may apply. Build a startup with a global student team. Applications for 2027 are open.
listing.eligibility: High-school students aged 14–18 worldwide. Selective admission; parental or guardian agreement is required for minors. Full-time participation over five weeks. Applications may close before the final deadline if the program fills.
listing.cost: US$7,495 listed tuition; application fees may apply

listing.title: Yale Young Global Scholars — Summer 2027
listing.description: Residential two-week summer program at Yale in New Haven, Connecticut, USA, with June and July 2027 sessions. Tuition is US$7,500 plus a US$100 regular-decision application fee; travel costs extra. Need-based aid and application fee waivers are available. Canadian students may apply. Regular-decision applications remain open until January 6, 2027, at 11:59 p.m. Eastern.
listing.location: Yale University, New Haven, Connecticut, USA
listing.eligibility: Ages 16–18 by July 18, 2027; current high-school sophomores or juniors (grades 10–11 or international equivalent), graduating in May/June 2028 or 2029 in the Northern Hemisphere. Strong English, first-time YYGS participation and parent/guardian involvement are required. Applicants from all countries, including Canada, are accepted.
listing.cost: US$7,500 tuition + US$100 application; travel extra
listing.hours: One residential two-week session in June or July 2027

listing.title: Diamond Challenge — 2027 entrepreneurship competition
listing.description: Global high-school entrepreneurship competition with business and social-innovation tracks. listing.description: Free online mentoring platform connecting junior developers and learners with experienced programmers worldwide. Browse available mentors and discuss coding skills, questions and career direction. The public mentor feed currently confirms available mentors; response, scheduling and a suitable match remain subject to each mentor.
listing.eligibility: Open to anyone, anywhere according to the official mentoring guidelines. No minimum age is stated; minors should confirm platform and parent/guardian requirements. Choose a mentor relevant to your skill level and goals.

listing.title: Start and lead a Hack Club at your school
listing.description: Apply to start a student-led coding club at your high school. Grants and rewards have separate conditions and are not guaranteed.
listing.eligibility: High-school students in a worldwide network of clubs. Hack Club's core programs serve ages 13–18. Coordinate school requirements with a teacher and review parent/guardian consent and the code of conduct.

text: worldwide network of high school coding clubs
